details: Sbaitso ( SPAYT-soh) is an artificial intelligence speech synthesis program released in 1991 by Creative Labs in Singapore for MS-DOS-based personal computers. The name is an acronym for "SoundBlaster Acting Intelligent Text-to-Speech Operator."

explainer.lead: Dr. Sbaitso is a text-to-speech program released by Creative Labs in Singapore in 1991 for MS-DOS personal computers. It is an early example of consumer PC software designed to turn written text into synthesized speech.

tiers.eli5: Imagine typing a sentence into a computer and having the computer say it out loud. That is what Dr. Sbaitso was made to do on MS-DOS computers. Its unusual name stands for “SoundBlaster Acting Intelligent Text-to-Speech Operator.”
tiers.practitioner: Treat Dr. Sbaitso as a legacy MS-DOS text-to-speech program, not a modern library or network service. Its original setting is Creative Labs’ 1991 release for MS-DOS-based personal computers, with written text as input and synthesized speech as output.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, Dr. Sbaitso implements a text-to-speech mapping from written text to synthesized speech. It was released by Creative Labs in Singapore in 1991 for MS-DOS-based personal computers; “Sbaitso” expands to “SoundBlaster Acting Intelligent Text-to-Speech Operator.”

explainer.example: On an MS-DOS PC, a user could give Dr. Sbaitso a sentence such as “Hello, world” and have the program produce synthesized speech for that text.

usedIn.name: MS-DOS personal computers
usedIn.detail: The program was released for this platform in 1991.

usedIn.name: Text-to-speech applications
usedIn.detail: Its stated role was to operate as a speech-synthesis program.

explainer.intuition: The basic idea is to give a computer written words and receive spoken output. Dr. Sbaitso packaged that idea as a named program for MS-DOS PCs.
howItWorks: A user supplies written text to the program on an MS-DOS-based personal computer.
Dr. Sbaitso acts as the text-to-speech operator described by its acronym.
Its speech-synthesis function turns the text into spoken output.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides a concrete 1991 example of text-to-speech software for personal computers. Its acronym also directly connects the program with Creative Labs’ Sound Blaster naming.
misconceptions: Dr. Sbaitso is software, not a human doctor or researcher.
It performs text-to-speech synthesis, not speech recognition.
“Sbaitso” is an acronym, not an arbitrary surname.

diagram.caption: Dr. Sbaitso runs on an MS-DOS PC and maps written text to synthesized speech.
